<b>Скелетная мышца</b> — орган из тысяч: A skeletal muscle is an organ made of thousands of fibers wrapped in a connective-tissue sheath, the epimysium. At the ends the collagen of the sheaths gathers into tendons that attach to bones. The body has ≈ 640 muscles.
<b>Пучок</b> (фасцикула) — десятки и сот: A fascicle is tens to hundreds of muscle fibers in their own sheath, the perimysium; between the fibers lies a thin endomysium with capillaries and nerves. Fascicles are the “grain” you see in meat.
<b>Мышечное волокно</b> — одна огромная: A muscle fiber is one huge cell up to 10–30 cm long and 10–100 µm thick. It formed by fusion of many cells, so it has hundreds of nuclei pushed to its membrane (the sarcolemma). Inside are myofibrils and mitochondria.
<b>Миофибрилла</b> — тяж из повторяющихс: A myofibril is a strand of repeating units, sarcomeres. Dark A bands (where the thick myosin filaments lie) alternate with light I bands (thin actin filaments only) — hence the cross-striation.
<b>Саркомер</b> (≈ 2,5 мкм в покое) — от: A sarcomere (≈ 2.5 µm at rest) runs from one Z line to the next. Thin actin filaments are anchored to the Z lines; thick myosin filaments with heads lie in the middle. The light center of the A band is the H zone, where the filaments do not overlap.
<b>Покой.</b> Ионов Ca²⁺ в цитоплазме ма: Rest. There is little Ca²⁺ in the cytoplasm: binding sites on actin are covered by the proteins tropomyosin and troponin, so myosin heads cannot attach. The sarcomere is ≈ 2.5 µm.
<b>Сокращение — скольжение нитей.</b> Ca: Contraction — sliding filaments. Ca²⁺ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum binds troponin and the sites on actin open. Myosin heads attach, pull toward the center (power stroke) and detach after splitting ATP. The filaments do not shorten — they slide: Z lines move closer, the I band and H zone narrow, the A band stays the same.
<b>Нет АТФ — окоченение.</b> Головка отц: No ATP — rigor. A head lets go of actin only after a new ATP molecule binds to it. Without ATP the cross-bridges freeze and the muscle turns stiff. This is rigor mortis, which sets in a few hours after death.
<b>Сигнал от нерва.</b> В нервно-мышечно: Signal from the nerve. At the neuromuscular junction acetylcholine is released; an action potential arises on the sarcolemma, runs both ways and dives inward along the T tubules, where it releases Ca²⁺. Slow (red) fibers: many mitochondria, myoglobin and capillaries; they work for a long time — posture, marathon.
<b>Быстрые (белые) волокна</b>: мало мит: Fast (white) fibers: few mitochondria and little myoglobin, energy mostly from glycolysis. They contract strongly and quickly but tire soon — sprint, jump. The mix of fiber types differs between people and partly changes with training.
Любое движение — от моргания до спринта: Every movement — from a blink to a sprint — is billions of tiny myosin “oars” pulling actin filaments. We go down from the muscle to the sarcomere and watch it contract.
\n <div><h2>Строение</h2>\n:
Structure

Muscle → fascicles (perimysium) → muscle fibers (endomysium) → myofibrils → sarcomeres. The connective-tissue sheaths continue into tendons. A fiber is a multinucleated syncytium; its supply of nuclei is topped up by satellite cells, which also repair the muscle after exercise.

Contraction

Nerve → acetylcholine → action potential along the sarcolemma and T tubules → Ca²⁺ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum → Ca²⁺ on troponin shifts tropomyosin → myosin cross-bridges with actin → power stroke powered by ATP. Relaxation: a pump returns Ca²⁺ (also using ATP).

Energy

Stored ATP lasts seconds; then creatine phosphate (≈ 10 s), glycolysis (minutes, see “Glycolysis”) and oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria (hours, see “ATP”).

Medicine

Myasthenia gravis — antibodies against acetylcholine receptors; curare-like muscle relaxants in anesthesia; cramps with low calcium and magnesium (see “Calcium”); muscular dystrophies — defects of the protein dystrophin.

Conventions

  • Levels are shown side by side, not nested; numbers of fibers and myofibrils are greatly reduced, proportions are schematic.
  • The sarcomere has 9 thick and 24 thin filaments (in reality a hexagonal lattice of thousands); tropomyosin, troponin, titin and nebulin are not drawn.
  • Sarcomere shortening (2.5 → 2.0 µm) and myosin head motion are sped up.
